turn_text: Alright, let's talk about this bill that you have some legislation that you wish to put in. You've been working with also with Senator Klobuchar. It concerns adding fire sprinkler systems to public housing. And if our listeners will recall a couple of years ago, there was a tragic incident at Cedar High Apartments. And this bill, this is not the first time you've been working on this, though.

You're right. This is yesterday, Senator Klobuchar and I reintroduced this bill. We first wrote it in response to the terrible tragedy in the Cedar High Apartments, as you mentioned, which is an apartment complex in Minneapolis. Five lives were lost in this fire. And the tragedy is that in this public apartment building, there was no sprinkler system. So people were just trapped there. And Senator Klobuchar and I went to work on this, and we introduced legislation that would help to retrofit these buildings with sprinkler systems, the older apartment buildings. And I guess there are over 100 and 40 of them in Minnesota that were built before there was a requirement to have sprinklers are just not up to par. It's not acceptable that people would be living in unsafe conditions. And you know, a lot of the folks that live in these apartment buildings are elders and people living with disabilities. So they are at particular risk. I'm very hopeful that we're going to be able to get this passed. We worked on it last year. And I've actually spoken directly with the new Secretary of Housing and Urban Development, Marcia Fudge, to urge her to have this be a priority in the Biden-Harris budget this year. So we're going to work hard to get it done. It needs to get done.

turn_text: Now, I understand there are some dollars attached to this, some grant money attached to this as well.
